trans-unit.source: Typ kontaktu/péče: hospitalizace, ambulantní vyšetření, multidisciplinární porada, telemedicína apod. Možno doplnit automatizovaně z NIS podle kódů výkonů.
trans-unit.target:
The setting in which the care took place. Options include:
•	Inpatient admission: patient admission to the centre for a period greater than one day.
•	Outpatient visit: scheduled visit made by the patient to a health service for diagnosis, treatment and / or follow-up of their illness. This does not involve a formal admission.
•	Multidisciplinary consultation: a multidisciplinary consultation is a process during which the patient is seen or discussed by several healthcare professionals from different disciplines to better coordinate clinical care.
o	MDT: multidisciplinary team meetings (MDTs) bring together healthcare professionals from different disciplines whose skills and knowledge are relevant to the patient’s condition and are essential for making decisions in line with scientific best practice and evidence. During MDTs, patient cases are discussed collectively. Decisions that are taken are recorded and are subsequently explained to the patient.
o	CPMS: Clinical Patient Management System (CPMS) is a virtual platform that brings together rare disease experts from one or several European Reference Networks to provide diagnostic and/or therapeutic advice on a clinical case.
•	Day admission: multidisciplinary medical care concentrated over a less than 24-hour period, not requiring full hospitalisation but also unable to be carried out on an outpatient basis.
•	Expert advice on medical record: a medical professional seeks the opinion of one or more healthcare professionals based on their training or specialised expertise. The patient is typically not present. This includes opinions given by electronic correspondence or telephone.
•	Consultation in another ward: a healthcare professional gives an opinion on the case of a patient they consult outside their own department.
•	Teleconsultation: the purpose of teleconsultation is to enable a medical professional to consult with a patient remotely. Another healthcare professional may be present with the patient and, if necessary, assist the primary medical professional during the teleconsultation.
•	Other context: the healthcare activity performed does not fall within any of the contexts mentioned above.

This data element is Not Mandatory

The recommended data standard is EHDSEpisodeOfCare.type
•	https://www.xt-ehr.eu/fhir/models/0.2.1/StructureDefinition-EHDSEpisodeOfCare-definitions.html#key_EHDSEpisodeOfCare.type

trans-unit.source: Např. diagnóza, management onemocnění, prenatální diagnostika, edukace pacienta, výzkum apod.
trans-unit.target:
Clinical goals for the care episode (diagnostic workup, disease management, rehabilitation, follow-up).

This data element is Not Mandatory

The recommended data standard is EHDSEncounter.admission.reason via SNOMED CT.
•	https://www.xt-ehr.eu/fhir/models/0.2.1/StructureDefinition-EHDSEncounter-definitions.html#key_EHDSEncounter.admission.reason[x]

If SNOMED CT not available, consider the following alternatives as choices:

•	Diagnosis: Determining the nature of a disease or distinguishing between one disease and other alternatives. An assessment may be made through a physical examination, laboratory tests or other investigation techniques.
•	Disease Management: Definition of strategies to be adopted for the care of the patient (preventive or therapeutic programme).
•	Follow-up: The activity is part of a scheduled review of the patient.
•	Genetic counselling: Advising families of the risks of birth defects, so that they can make an informed decision about a current or future pregnancy.
•	Prenatal diagnosis: Determining the nature of a pathological condition or disease in an embryo, post-implantation foetus, or pregnant woman.
•	Pre-implantation diagnosis: determining the nature of a pathological condition or disease in an egg, zygote or blastocyst before implantation. A cytogenetic analysis can detect the presence or absence of a genetic disease.
•	Emergency care: first aid or other immediate intervention provided in the event of an accident or health condition that requires urgent attention before any definitive medical and surgical care can be administered.
•	Medical procedure: therapeutic procedures, surgical procedures, prescriptions, etc.
•	Research protocol: activity as part of a research protocol carried out outside the usual framework of patient care (cohort, clinical trial, etc.).
•	Therapeutic education: teaching or training patients about their own health needs.
•	Other: The objective of care does not fall within any of the contexts mentioned above.

trans-unit.source: Profese zapojených poskytovatelů péče: lékař, psycholog, fyzioterapeut, dietolog, atd.
trans-unit.target:
Role or profession of the person delivering care.

This data element is Not Mandatory

The recommended data standard is EHDSHealthProfessional.professionalRole.role via SNOMED CT.
•	https://www.xt-ehr.eu/fhir/models/0.2.1/StructureDefinition-EHDSHealthProfessional-definitions.html#key_EHDSHealthProfessional.professionalRole.role

If SNOMED CT not available, consider the following alternatives as choices:

•	Social worker: the social worker helps patients and their families with the formalities involved in obtaining benefits and assistance: administrative, social, financial etc.
•	Dietitian: a dietary specialist who provides nutritional advice and educates patients with metabolic and / or eating difficulties.
•	Occupational therapist: occupational therapists assess the patient’s lifestyle and optimise their environment to help reduce disability and assure safe activities of daily living.
•	Physiotherapist: Physiotherapists perform massage and physical therapy with the aim of maintaining, rehabilitating or preventing the deterioration of a patient’s functional abilities.
•	Psychologist: Psychological professional who supports the mental health of patients through the different stages of their illness.
•	Psychomotor therapist: these therapists help patients suffering from psychomotor disorders by optimising their psychomotor functions: attention difficulties, problems with spatial awareness, etc.
•	Genetic counsellor: In conjunction with the geneticist and other physicians treating the patient, genetic counsellors explain the potential risks of passing the disease on to family members and assist in family planning.
•	Nurse: the nurse provides care designed to maintain or restore the health of a sick person by regularly monitoring the health of patients during their hospitalisation and often during discharge process.
•	Speech therapist: the speech therapist prevents, assesses and treats voice and articulation disorders, communication disorders, speech disorders, oropharyngeal swallowing disorders, as well as other disorders associated with understanding and expressing language. 
•	Specialist teacher: the specialised teacher prepares and leads training courses for young people with disabilities (hearing, visual, etc.), ensuring their educational progress.
•	Physician: holder of a licence to practise medicine
•	Other paramedical: other paramedical profession not mentioned above.
